what: The rows of the Open with menu: openersFor (npm SDK) and openers_for (Python package) on the same cases. Every expected row is written by hand. The same bytes in both packages; each test holds this file's sha256.
keys: tools names a list in lists; kind is world or element; address is what parseOwLink reads or elementAddress takes; surface is the options object with snake_case keys (signed_in), which the npm test spells signedIn. expect is the rows in order, each {id, name, href, state}; refuse is the refusal: error address with the address error's reason, or error type (a TypeError) whose message names names (spelt signedIn in the npm test), with its kind: unknown_key, a key the object does not take, refused by name; bad_value, a key it takes whose value it refuses, a missing value included. Each package tells the two apart by its own message, so a reader that refuses a known key as unknown fails the case. options, when present, is the fifth argument as written ({element}: the element as served, the mark flat on it); a row whose open.element_skips names a mark the element carries is not there. A row whose open.element_types is a list that does not hold the address's type word is not there on an element's menu, and a world's menu reads no element types.
